name: Fredun Pharmaceuticals Ltd
title: Fredun Pharmaceuticals Ltd - 539730 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Fredun guides 25-30% top-line growth for FY27 with margin expansion, but working capital stress and rising debt cost remain; no supply-side capacity discipline, instead capacity adds (12-13 packing lines, new wing).

capex.quote: we are adding another 12 to 13 packing lines by end of September. We will have -- we are also going to construct a new wing within the plant.

triggers.label: FY27 top-line growth 25-30%
triggers.quote: We can consider a growth and overall growth of around 25% to 30% on our top line from the last year.

triggers.label: Inventory INR270 cr on INR700 cr top line
triggers.quote: Now at around INR700 crores, we still have only INR270 crores, and our cash flows have constantly improved.

triggers.label: Working capital stress persists

triggers.quote: Few percentage, 1% or 2%, the buyer absorbs sometimes certain products we have to absorb

summary.headline: Fredun Pharma Q4 FY26 total income rose 27.27% YoY to INR213 crore, EBITDA margin expanded 326 bps to 13.67%, and management guides 25-30% FY27 top-line growth.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 total income was INR213 crore (up 27.27% YoY), EBITDA INR29.13 crore (up 67.05%, margin 13.67%, +326 bps) and net profit INR11.07 crore (up 56.47%). For FY26, total income was INR639.12 crore (up 40.08%), EBITDA INR94.79 crore (margin 14.83%, +276 bps) and net profit INR33.21 crore (up 59.59%). Management said new-age businesses (pet care, mobility, nutraceuticals, cosmetics, hormones, anti-aging) carry higher gross margins and are growing 40-50% CAGR, while vintage business grows 10-20%. Management guided to 25-30% top-line growth for FY27 and said margins will keep rising for about 8 quarters before a spike. Working capital and finance cost were the main investor concerns.

financial_highlights.change: +27.27% YoY vs INR167.41 crore in Q4 FY25

segments.name: Vintage business (pharma, exports, institutional, tolling, third-party branding, Fredun DC)
segments.commentary: Growing 15-20% YoY per management (later said 10-15% on cruise control); exports about INR110-120 crore, tolling about INR24 crore, indirect exports/institution sales about INR120-130 crore, third-party branding INR45-50 crore, Fredun DC INR25-30 crore. Over 1,000 registrations pending.

segments.name: Pet care
segments.commentary: About INR42-43 crore of FY26 sales; 42 functional food biscuit variants being launched; Wagr.in e-commerce/pet portal soft launch expected late June to early July 2026.

segments.name: Mobility (BraceOn, DigiOn, NebOn, Mobilitics)
segments.commentary: About INR29-30 crore of FY26 sales; management targets INR100 crore run-rate in 2-2.5 years and INR250-300 crore in 5-7 years. Mobilitics (physiotherapy) targeted at INR30-40 crore in two years; growing 55-60% CAGR per management.

segments.name: Nutraceuticals
segments.commentary: About INR26 crore of FY26 sales per management.

segments.name: Cosmetics (mass market)
segments.commentary: About INR20-22 crore of FY26 sales; dermaceutics gross margins cited at 80-90%.

segments.name: Hormones and anti-aging (launch)
segments.commentary: Two new lines being launched via doctor channel, starting in MMRDA region and metros; NAD+ manufacturing and exclusive API import rights cited. Hormone gross margin cited at around 50%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth of 25-30% over FY26 targeted; management says run-rate is in line and it could do better.
EBITDA/PAT margin expected to keep rising for about 8 quarters, then a sudden profit spike once new-age demographic reach saturates (about 7-8 quarters, or 2.5-3 years per another answer).
Long-term PAT target of 10-12% in the next few years on a 2-3x top line.
Mix goal: new-age business to reach about 50% of revenue within the next few years, and about 70:30 within 2-3 years after that; transition to consumer company over 7-8 years.
Management expects finance-cost percentage to fall within 3-4 years as ratios improve.
Pet care goal: products across a pet's life by 2032-33; a first-in-India formulation in Stage 4 trials expected within 12 months.
capex_capacity: About 43 manufacturing locations; around 80% or more of products made in-house, with contract manufacturing used for wheelchairs, braces and sterile products (liquid injections, PFS, dry powder injections, beta-lactams).
12-13 additional packing lines to be added by end-September 2026.
A new wing to be constructed within the existing plant; no capex amount or timeline given beyond the packing lines.
Management targets top-3 or top-4 manufacturing capacity at one location within 2.5 years; cluster of 4 plants at one location.
Facilities being set up for functional foods, with plans for wet pet food manufacturing.
demand_pricing: Order book of about INR320-330 crore in hand, equal to 6-7 months of orders, per management.

Raw material costs rose due to Middle East/geopolitical tensions and petroleum-linked inputs; management said 3-4 months of buffer stock shielded margins, with a 1-2% cost absorbed by buyers on some products.
Some products repriced upward; management said price increases were passed through and that the impact on bottom line is nil.
Vintage business growth 15-20% per one answer and 10-15% per another; new-age growth 40-50% CAGR from a smaller base.
Mobility competitors named as Visco and Timo; management claims no online-brand exposure and an offline-only distribution model.

qa_highlights.question: Growth plan for the hormone and anti-aging launches (Keshav Toshniwal).
qa_highlights.answer: Two lines launching via doctor channel, starting MMRDA and metros, with online sales of medicated hormone products planned; NAD+ manufacturing and exclusive API import rights cited; CDSCO rule limiting prescribing to certified doctors seen as favourable.

qa_highlights.question: Mobility scale-up strategy (Vinod Shah).
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 mobility sales about INR30 crore; INR100 crore run-rate targeted in 2-2.5 years; distribution to match Maharashtra in 17-18 states within 2.5 years; Mobilitics physiotherapy pre-bookings full.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material inflation and demand slowdown from geopolitics (Ankit).
qa_highlights.answer: Management said price rises were absorbed by buffer stock and passed through; 1-2% absorbed on some products; no impact to bottom line; orders ahead of six to seven months.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue split between vintage and new-age businesses (Nikhil Agarwal).
qa_highlights.answer: Vintage contributes most FY26 revenue (exports INR110-120 crore, institutional INR120-130 crore, third-party branding INR45-50 crore); new-age includes pet care INR42-43 crore, mobility INR29-30 crore, nutraceuticals INR26 crore, cosmetics INR20-22 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify FY27 growth (Nishita Shanklesha).
qa_highlights.answer: Management intends 25-30% top-line growth over FY26, says run-rate supports it, and notes a history of under-promising and over-delivering.

qa_highlights.question: Finance cost and debt (Keshav Toshniwal).
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged rates are higher, said absolute debt will rise with scale, and expects the cost percentage to decline over the next 3-4 years; debt serviced comfortably.

qa_highlights.question: Free cash flow and working capital (Devang Shah).
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory is INR270 crore against about INR700 crore revenue (vs INR220 crore on INR450 crore earlier); operating cash flow now positive; debt-to-equity 0.8; more working capital and debt may be needed for growth.

risks_watch: Working capital intensity: inventory of about INR270 crore; management concedes working capital and debt needs will rise with growth.
Finance cost: management acknowledged higher interest rates; absolute debt expected to rise before ratios improve.
Geopolitical raw-material inflation: petroleum-linked inputs rising; pass-through of 1-2% cost absorbed by buyers on some products.
Pet care Wagr.in launch slipping repeatedly (earlier mid-June, now late June to early July); management acknowledged a 3-4 month delay.
Margin path depends on new-age mix, with management's 10-12% PAT projection still lacking a timeline beyond a few years.
Unquantified figures: the stated 1,000+ pending registrations and the ambiguity between 8-quarter and 2.5-3 year margin timelines.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional, with broad claims on margins, growth and new categories (hormones, anti-aging, pet care, mobility) and limited hard data. Cautious only on finance cost and working capital, which management addressed by pointing to positive operating cash flow and a planned strategy.
key_quotes: We can consider a growth and overall growth of around 25% to 30% on our top line from the last year.
Last 19 years, our growth is a 32% CAGR. There's not a single year of degrowth in the last 19 years.
Working capital is not a worry for us right now.
We are not a inorganic growth Pet Care company where we are spending money to sell our products.

adds.what: New wing to be constructed within existing plant (no capex or timeline given)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 top-line growth of 25-30% (midpoint 27.5%), backed by a INR320-330 crore order book (6-7 months of orders), 12-13 packing lines due by end-September 2026, and new-age lines growing 40-50%; the backing is partly specific but lacks capex figures and detailed timing for the new wing.
